Later, Google Calendar's updateEvent/deleteEvent use `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`, which returns undefined when externalCalendarId is undefined (previously the code fell back to a single calendar's externalId).

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/core/EventManager.ts` `createAllCalendarEvents`, when iterating `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)`, the `else` branch for `!destination.credentialId` calls `createEvent(c, event)` without passing the destination’s `externalId`. After this diff, `createEvent` returns `{ externalId, credentialId }`, and downstream code in `EventManager` now uses `result.externalId` to populate `externalCalendarId` in booking references. Since `externalId` is never provided here, it will be `undefined`, so the stored reference lacks `externalCalendarId`, which can break later update/delete that rely on it. This is directly visible in the diff: the credentialId branch uses `createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId)` but the no-credentialId branch does not.
